questions.q: In "फेरीवाले उलहनी," identify two specific time markers and two specific place markers that establish the physical setting of the opening scene.
questions.a: Correct answer: Time markers — "शाम" (evening) and "अंधेरा घिरने लगा" (darkness gathering); Place markers — "सड़क के किनारे" (roadside) and "फुटपाथ पर" (on the pavement). A wrong answer (e.g., saying "morning" or "inside a shop") reveals the student cannot distinguish explicit textual evidence from assumptions, or confuses the opening scene with later scenes. This indicates a literal comprehension gap — the student needs practice locating explicit setting details before analyzing their effect.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the writer uses sensory details (sight, sound, smell) in the first three paragraphs to create an atmosphere of tired persistence rather than hopelessness.
questions.a: Correct answer: The writer combines visual details ("थकी आँखें," "मैले कपड़े") with auditory details ("आवाज़ में थकान नहीं," "स्पष्ट उच्चारण") and the smell of "तेल और मसालों" to show a vendor who is physically worn but professionally sharp — the sensory mix creates dignity, not defeat. A wrong answer focusing only on "sadness" or "poverty" reveals the misconception that atmosphere = single emotion; the student misses how contrasting sensory layers (tired body + alert voice) build complex atmosphere. This shows the student reads for plot, not textual texture.

questions.q: Apply the concept of "atmosphere shift" to the moment when लखपत enters the scene. Quote one line before and one line after his entry, then explain how the atmosphere changes using specific words from the text.
questions.a: Correct answer: Before: "फेरीवाला अपनी धुन में मगन था" (vendor absorbed in his rhythm) — atmosphere: calm, routine. After: "लखपत ने कड़ककर पूछा" (Lakhpat asked sharply) — atmosphere: tense, confrontational. Shift created by "कड़ककर" (sharply) replacing "मगन" (absorbed), and interrogative tone replacing declarative. A wrong answer that only says "it gets tense" without quoting words reveals the student cannot link linguistic choices to atmospheric effect — they generalize instead of analyzing textual evidence.

questions.q: Analyze how the physical setting of the "नुक्कड़ की चाय की दुकान" (corner tea stall) functions as more than background — how does it structure the social interactions and power dynamics between उलहनी, लखपत, and जक्सी?
questions.a: Correct answer: The tea stall is a semi-public space where hierarchies play out: लखपत (authority figure) stands, उलहनी (vendor) sits lower on "पटरी," जक्सी (observer) leans — vertical positioning mirrors social power. The stall's "काँच के जार" (glass jars) and "बेंच" create physical barriers/territories. A wrong answer treating the stall as mere backdrop ("they just talk there") reveals the student misses how setting *organizes* character relationships — a senior-secondary error of ignoring spatial semantics in narrative.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "The evening setting in 'फेरीवाले उलहनी' is merely a temporal backdrop; the story would work equally well at noon." Defend your judgment with three textual arguments.
questions.a: Correct answer: The claim is false. Argument 1: "अंधेरा घिरने लगा" creates urgency — vendors must sell before total darkness, raising stakes. Argument 2: Evening shadows ("छायाएँ लंबी होती गईं") visually mirror the moral ambiguity लखपत introduces. Argument 3: The "शाम की भीड़" (evening crowd) — tired workers, returning students — forms a specific audience that witnesses the confrontation, making it public accountability, not private dispute. A wrong answer agreeing with the claim reveals the student treats setting as decorative, not functional — a fundamental misreading of narrative craft.

questions.q: Create a 4-line atmospheric paragraph describing a street vendor's setting at a different time of day (early morning OR late night), using at least three sensory details and one word that establishes emotional tone. Do not name the time directly — let the details imply it.
questions.a: Good answer example (early morning): "धुंध में लिपटी सड़क पर ठंडी भाप उठती चाय की गंध के साथ मिलती है; साइकिल की घंटी की टुन-टुन और अखबार के पन्नों की सरसराहट के बीच, एक अकेला ठेला अपनी रोशनी आप ही जलाता है — आशा, थकान से भारी नहीं." (Uses smell, sound, sight; "आशा" establishes tone; implies dawn without naming it.) A poor answer ("Morning time vendor sells tea. It is cold and quiet.") reveals the student cannot "show, not tell" — they lack the skill to construct atmosphere through sensory layering, only summarize.
